symptom: `SQL <alias> GENERATE CONNECTOR INTO <Module>` silently omitted every object whose own NAME contains a dot. On a DuckGraphLake lake the raw topic tables are named after the Kafka topic (`main."local__cdc.CdcPublish.Customer.1.local"`), so 4 of the 9 listed objects were missing from the output, with no warning and no error -- the only warnings printed were about unmappable columns (ako/mxcli#2422).
cause: the address was flattened to one string by qualifiedTableName and split again by splitTableName, which took the last two dot-separated parts: schema `1`, name `local`. DescribeTable then found nothing and readListed's `continue` discarded the error. Two more faults sat behind that one, each of which would have turned the silent drop into silently invalid output: TableSchema.QualifiedName joined the parts unquoted, so the emitted SQL would have been `FROM main.local__cdc.CdcPublish.Customer.1.local` (`syntax error at or near ".1."`), and toPascalCase treated only `_ - space` as separators, so TableToEntityName gave `LocalCdc.cdcpublish.customer.1.local` -- dots and all -- which is not a Mendix entity name.
file: sql/meta.go (splitQualifiedIdent, quoteIdent/needsQuoting, splitTableName); sql/schema.go (QualifiedName, qualifiedTableName, readListed returns what it skipped); sql/naming.go (toPascalCase: `.` is a separator, in both the early return and the loop); sql/generate.go (GenerateResult.SkippedObjects); mdl/executor/cmd_sql.go (reports them); test sql/generate_dotted_names_2422_test.go
insight: Fixing the addressing ALONE would have been worse than the bug: the object would have been generated with an entity name containing dots and a FROM clause that is a syntax error, where before it was merely absent. Check what the name becomes, not just whether the object is found -- `TableToEntityName` had a second, easily missed trap, an early return for names without `_` or `-` that only capitalises the first letter, so `my.table` became `My.table` and never reached the separator loop. Quote only what needs it (anything outside [A-Za-z0-9_], or a leading digit): quoting every identifier would change every query the tool has ever generated, and a bare reserved word needs no quoting once it is schema-qualified, which ako/mxcli#2414 measured. Three one-line probes settle the whole diagnosis on any such database: `select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema='main' and table_name='<dotted>'` (7 -- the metadata side is fine), the same select quoted (5 rows), and unquoted (syntax error). Four controls, each failing a different test: split on every dot -> SplitTableName_QuotedNameKeepsItsDots; quoteIdent never quotes -> QualifiedName_QuotesANameThatNeedsIt; `.` not a separator -> TableToEntityName_DotsAreWordSeparators; skipped list dropped -> UnreadableObjectIsReported. Live result: 5 of 9 objects generated before, 9 of 9 after, all 9 queries running.
